chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun from Muhammad ibn Harun al-Jallab who said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: When injustice becomes more overwhelming than the truth, it is not permissible for anyone to think good of anyone else until he recognizes that good from him.
ai.seo_question: When should a Muslim stop assuming the best about others according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes a principle of *al-zann bi-l-khass* (specific assumption) over *al-zann bi-l-amm* (general assumption), noting that when injustice (*jawr*) becomes dominant, the default presumption of innocence (*al-sihha*) is suspended. This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on verifying character through direct evidence rather than relying on social reputation during eras of moral decay, ensuring that one's judgment remains precise and just.
